title: Lattice Function
body_html:
Lattice Function

This node is the foundation layer for lattice functions and buildings. It should be used by both epipelagic and supercuspidal nodes instead of the older epipelagic_theta.lattice_function.

Let \(V\) be a right \(D\)-vector space. A lattice function \(\mathscr L\) on \(V\) assigns to each real number \(s\) an \(\mathfrak o_D\)-lattice \(\mathscr L_s\), decreasing in \(s\), compatible with scalar translation, and left-continuous: \[ \mathscr L_t \subseteq \mathscr L_s \quad(s<t), \qquad \mathscr L_{s+\nu(d)}=\mathscr L_s\, d, \qquad \mathscr L_s=\bigcap_{t<s} \mathscr L_t. \] One writes \[ \mathscr L_{r+}=\bigcup_{t>r}\mathscr L_t,\qquad \operatorname{Jump}(\mathscr L)=\{r\in \mathbb R: \mathscr L_r\ne \mathscr L_{r+}\}. \]

The lattice function induces filtrations on \(\operatorname{End}_D(V)\) and \(\operatorname{GL}_D(V)\) by requiring operators or group elements to shift every \(\mathscr L_s\) into \(\mathscr L_{s+r}\).

In the paper, lattice functions are interchangeable with splittable \(D\)-norms via \(\mathscr L_r=\ell^{-1}([r,\infty))\). The symbol \(\mathscr L\) denotes the function; \(\mathscr L_s\) is a single lattice (its value at level \(s\)).

When a lattice function is attached to a point \(x\) of the building (the Broussous-Stevens point-to-norm bijection; see Self-Dual Lattice Function), we write \(\mathscr L_x\) for the function and \(\mathscr L_{x,r}:=\mathscr L_x(r)\) for its value at level \(r\), with \(\mathscr L_{x,0}\) and \(\mathscr L_{x,0+}\) at levels \(0\) and \(0^+\). The level subscript carries the point: different points of one facet share the same lattice chain but give different functions \(\mathscr L_x\).
